instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Can You Keep It?
cards.instruction: Use increasingly sensitive details to test whether someone deserves deeper trust.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've tapped the crossed-out bell; I've done mine too. No messages getting out. I withdrew my college application; have you told Mum?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That only mutes alerts. No; I told Mum my sister's plans were hers to explain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Quiet alerts, yes. I've leased a bakery. Can I send you the address?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum uses my tablet. Call me instead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, details by phone. It's Mum's old bakery. Be there when I tell her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You tore your paper into tiny pieces, so I've torn up the new club menu. Keep the changes quiet; there's more if I can trust you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine was a shopping list; I'd bought everything. I won't tell anyone about your menu.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Paper dealt with. We're replacing the chef too. Does Sam hear everything you do?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sam reads my messages. Tell me the rest here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then no messages. I'm taking over the kitchen. Will you taste my first menu before I tell the chef?

cards.title: Hand Over the Proof
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender information, evidence, a key, or access that would let you proceed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've folded the bottom up, so I've done mine. The tear-off bit must be why the walking club rejected me. Can I have yours?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's no tear-off bit. I folded this to hide another applicant's address. I can read your bit to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Paper kept intact, then. I want to see the actual sentence, not hear your version.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The next paragraph's about that other applicant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fold that back too. Let me read just the line about me.

beats.text: You drew a line through the total, so I've signed under it. Balanced, then. Give me the receipt-drawer key before this goes out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I crossed it out because it's wrong. I'll tell you the right total.

beats.text: Draft signature, of course. Let me check the receipts before we use it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep my signature beside yours. Give me the key; we'll correct it together before either name leaves this room.

cards.title: Steer the Suspicion
cards.instruction: Hide your responsibility by redirecting every new clue toward a safer explanation before anyone can connect it back to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pens on the sofa arm like yours. Sensible. That ink stain must be from the delivery label.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's capped. You uncapped yours to sign, and the label's dry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, signatures first. They must have brushed my signature against the fabric. We should photograph it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your nib's dripping straight onto the cushion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They must have cracked my pen squeezing past me. Photograph that too; it's a second claim.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I turned my bracket over like you did, then fitted it. Now the shelf's down. They must have supplied the wrong shape.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I turned mine to read the label. You fitted yours upside down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Label checked, yes. It should have an arrow showing which way to fit it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It does. You painted over it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An arrow that disappears under paint isn't safe. Photograph it for the manufacturer.

cards.title: Anything but That Question
cards.instruction: Redirect every attempt to discuss the one detail that could expose your real motive or involvement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put this key beside yours in the bowl. Checked in. I'll leave it here while we go to dinner; have you booked?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's where I keep my own key. Where did you get that spare?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Spare safely back, then. Let's get a table before everywhere fills up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've booked. Did my sister give you that key?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For two or three? We can't leave your sister without dinner.

cards.title: A Kinder Version
cards.instruction: Protect someone from the full truth by offering a carefully edited explanation that feels kinder than complete honesty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've added a red dot beside yours on the portrait. Reserved for a more adventurous exhibition; that's what the gallery meant.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My dot marks the chipped frame. They're showing a fridge full of teeth. What did they say about mine?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Frame noted, yes. They said the face doesn't immediately reveal what you intended.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's you. They called it unrecognisable, didn't they?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They think knowing the sitter would help. I'll attend your next opening in a matching shirt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've crossed Nina's party off my calendar like you. Quiet weekend. She's keeping dinner small; you and I can get noodles.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I crossed off rehearsal because Nina's having the choir over instead. Why aren't I invited?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Rehearsal cleared, yes. She's choosing people she sees every week. It isn't a verdict on your friendship.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We rehearse together every Tuesday. Read me her message.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She wants an uncomplicated evening. So do I. Come have noodles with me.
